title: Private DR: add Postgres backup + PITR helpers (pg_dump + WAL archiving) and restore sequencing
author: Michael Nguyen
description:
Motivation: For Redwood Private DR we need a repeatable way to (a) take a consistent Postgres logical dump for control-plane state, and (b) optionally enable point-in-time restore (PITR) by archiving WAL segments to the configured backup repository. This PR introduces `rw-private-dr` helpers to generate pg_dump artifacts, validate WAL archiving configuration, and orchestrate Postgres restore steps as part of the broader control plane restore sequencing.

Scope:
- Add Postgres backup helpers: `postgres dump` (pg_dump custom format), `postgres dump-verify`, and manifest emission used by `backup create`.
- Add optional PITR support via WAL archiving configuration (archive_command + retention hints). This does NOT attempt to fully manage Postgres HA; it wires the minimal config + verification needed for operators to execute PITR in DR.
- Add restore sequencing logic: bring up Postgres first, restore DB state, run migrations check, then restore config/policy services and other control plane components in a deterministic order.
- Add guardrails: version checks, required extensions, connection validation, and clearer error messages for common operator mistakes (bad creds, missing repo path, WAL archive disabled).

Out of scope (follow-ups):
- Maintenance mode + API write blocking (tracked in ENG-4904; planned PR #901).
- Storage backend adapter work (S3/minio/etc.) is handled separately; this PR relies on the existing backup repo abstraction.

Operator-facing behavior:
- Default path remains dump-only backups using pg_dump.
- If `postgres.pitr.enabled=true`, we validate WAL archiving is configured and we will include WAL archive metadata in the backup manifest. Restore supports selecting either `--restore-type=dump` or `--restore-type=pitr` with `--target-time`.

Config changes (new keys):
- `postgres.backup.format`: `custom` (default) | `plain`
- `postgres.pitr.enabled`: boolean (default false)
- `postgres.pitr.wal_archive`: `auto` | `external`
- `postgres.pitr.target_time`: RFC3339 (restore-time only)

Example snippet (values merged into the generated dr plan):
- postgres:
  - pitr:
    - enabled: true
    - wal_archive: auto

Testing:
- Unit tests for config parsing + command construction.
- Integration test harness (kind) that runs pg_dump against a seeded DB and exercises `restore plan` sequencing (dump-restore path).

Notes:
- We intentionally use pg_dump (logical) for baseline backups due to portability across customer topologies. PITR uses WAL archiving only when the customer enables it and provides a repository with sufficient throughput/retention.

Docs:
- README updated with new subcommands and the PITR prerequisites checklist. Confluence runbooks will be updated in a follow-up once this lands (Docs already tracking in the Day-2 Ops outline).

review_conversation:
Ethan Park (review): The sequencing changes look good, but can you clarify what we consider the "ready" signal for Postgres before we attempt migrations checks? We had flakes in other installers.
Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. I switched the gate to: (1) TCP connect, (2) `SELECT 1`, (3) check `pg_is_in_recovery()` matches expected mode for dump vs PITR, and added a 10m timeout with backoff.

Diego Santos (review): For PITR, I’m worried about assuming we can write archive_command automatically. Some customers manage postgresql.conf via their own operator.
Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. Added `postgres.pitr.wal_archive=external` mode. In that mode we only validate that `archive_mode=on` and `archive_command` is non-empty, and we stop short of attempting to set it.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please add operator-friendly errors for the most common failure: WAL archive path permissions and missing repository connectivity. Also, can we record enough metadata in the manifest to make game day evidence capture easier?
Michael Nguyen (author): Added explicit checks for repo write permissions and included `pitr.enabled`, `wal_archive_mode`, and the last observed WAL segment name in the manifest. Also added structured log lines we can grep during drills.

Marcus Lin (review): Ensure we never log DB passwords or KMS material. I see one debug log printing the full conn string.
Michael Nguyen (author): Fixed. We now redact userinfo in connection strings and avoid printing env var values.

Hanae Suzuki (review): Restore step ordering: can we make policy/config service restore explicitly depend on Postgres migrations being complete?
Michael Nguyen (author): Yes—migrations check is now a hard gate. If migrations aren’t compatible, restore stops with guidance to use a matching installer version.

Final status: Approved after changes; squash merge.
release_notes:
- Private DR: add Postgres dump + optional PITR (WAL archiving) helpers to `rw-private-dr`
- Restore: deterministic control plane restore sequencing with readiness + compatibility gates
- Security: redact sensitive connection info in logs; stricter config validation for PITR prerequisites
